title: Apple Inc. (AAPL) Declares $0.73 Quarterly Dividend

Apple Inc. (AAPL) Declares $0.73 Quarterly Dividend Posted by Donald Scott | Aug 5th, 2018
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) announced a quarterly dividend on Tuesday, July 31st, RTT News reports. Shareholders of record on Monday, August 13th will be given a dividend of 0.73 per share by the iPhone maker on Thursday, August 16th. This represents a $2.92 annualized dividend and a yield of 1.40%. The ex-dividend date of this dividend is Friday, August 10th.
Apple has increased its dividend payment by an average of 10.1% per year over the last three years and has raised its dividend annually for the last 5 consecutive years. Apple has a dividend payout ratio of 25.6% meaning its dividend is sufficiently covered by earnings. Research analysts expect Apple to earn $13.04 per share next year, which means the company should continue to be able to cover its $2.92 annual dividend with an expected future payout ratio of 22.4%. AAPL opened at $207.99 on Friday. The company has a current ratio of 1.31, a quick ratio of 1.37 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.84. The firm has a market capitalization of $1,019.35 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 18.80, a PEG ratio of 1.64 and a beta of 1.16. Apple has a twelve month low of $149.16 and a twelve month high of $208.74.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last posted its earnings results on Tuesday, July 31st. The iPhone maker reported $2.34 earnings per share for the quarter, topping the Thomson Reuters’ consensus estimate of $2.18 by $0.16. Apple had a net margin of 21.98% and a return on equity of 43.50%. The company had revenue of $53.27 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $52.43 billion. During the same period last year, the business posted $1.67 earnings per share. The business’s revenue for the quarter was up 17.3% compared to the same quarter last year. research analysts predict that Apple will post 11.68 earnings per share for the current year.
Apple announced that its Board of Directors has approved a share repurchase program on Tuesday, May 1st that authorizes the company to buyback $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This buyback authorization authorizes the iPhone maker to purchase up to 11.9% of its stock through open market purchases. Stock buyback programs are typically an indication that the company’s leadership believes its stock is undervalued.
